catholic-encyclopedia-1913-acathistus-ak: This 1913 reference piece on the Akathistos — the great Byzantine hymn to the Virgin, sung standing. Hugh Henry unfolds its twenty-four stanzas. Constantinople sang it through sieges. The East's loveliest Marian praise. Choirs still sing it on Friday nights in Lent.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-agios-o-theos: A 1913 entry on Agios o Theos — Holy God, the opening of the Trisagion. Hugh Henry traces its liturgical glory. East and West sing the thrice-holy words. Constantinople's chant shook the city. The Church's holiest acclamation. Its chant opens the Byzantine liturgy.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-alexander-of-: This 1913 reference piece on Alexander of Abonoteichos — the pagan charlatan Lucian exposed. John Joseph A'Becket tells the fraud. His snake-god Glycon fooled the crowds. Satire killed what reason could not. Antiquity's most famous quack. His oracle answered the emperor's questions.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-alfonso-of-bu: A 1913 entry on Alfonso of Burgos — the converted rabbi turned bishop. Thomas Schwertner tells his remarkable change. His learning served the Spanish Church. The convert became a prelate. A soul that crossed the divide. His Scrutinium convinced many doubters. His baptism shocked the Spanish Jews.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-amorios: This 1913 reference piece on Amorios — Amorium, the Phrygian city, now a titular see. Its bishops grace the old lists. The Arabs sacked its proud walls. The Church keeps its ancient name. A see of old Asia Minor. Its mint struck the imperial coins.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-amos: This 1913 reference article on Amos — the herdsman prophet of Tekoa. Francis Gigot weighs his fiery book. Let justice roll like waters, he cried. His words shook the northern kingdom. The first writing prophet. His plumb line judged the nations. His book is the shepherd's thunder.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-antiphellos: This 1913 reference piece on Antiphellos — the Lycian city, now a titular see. Its bishops grace the old lists. The sea guards its ruined harbor. The Church keeps its ancient name. A see of the southern coast. Its tombs are cut in the cliffs.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-argos: A 1913 entry on Argos — the Greek city, now a titular see. Thomas Shahan notes its ancient fame. Its bishops graced the old lists. The Larissa hill crowns its plain. A see of the Peloponnese. Its theater is the Greeks' oldest.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-arsenius-auto: This 1913 reference piece on Arsenius Autorianus — the Patriarch of Constantinople. Mark McNeal tells his troubled tale. He excommunicated the emperor. The Arsenian schism bore his name. A patriarch against the throne. His schism troubled the empire's church. His tomb lies in the capital's church.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-august-wilhel: This 1913 reference piece on August Wilhelm Ambros — the historian of music. Joseph Otten honors his great Geschichte. His volumes traced music's long tale. Prague's conservatory knew his zeal. The chronicler of the musical art. His Bunte Blätter charmed the readers.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-barbalissos: This 1913 reference article on Barbalissos — the Syrian city, now a titular see. Siméon Vailhé notes its Christian past. Its bishops graced the old councils. The Euphrates guards its ruined site. A see of the eastern frontier. Its walls recall the Persian wars.
